questions.q: National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) is a joint venture of the Government of India and which group of states?
options: Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh
questions.explain: National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) is a Joint Venture (JV) of Government of India (GoI) with Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan and UP — the four National Capital Region (NCR) participating states.

questions.q: National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) works under which Union Ministry?
options: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
questions.explain: National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) is under Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), even though Railways is an equity partner.

questions.q: The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for setting up National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) was signed on:
questions.explain: Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) came first — 29 June 2011, between Government of India (GoI) and the four states. Incorporation came later, in 2013.

questions.q: National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) was incorporated on:
questions.explain: Incorporation was 21 August 2013; 29 June 2011 was the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) and 20 Oct 2023 the first service.

questions.q: Under which Act was National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) incorporated?
questions.explain: The book records incorporation under the Companies Act, 1956.

questions.q: Cabinet approval for National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) came in:
questions.explain: Cabinet approval was July 2013, just before incorporation in August 2013.

questions.q: The seed capital of National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) was:
questions.explain: National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) started with a seed capital of Rs. 100 crore.

questions.q: Government of India's total equity share in National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) is:
questions.explain: Government of India (GoI) holds 50%; the four states together hold the other 50%.

questions.q: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)'s share within the Government of India equity is:
questions.explain: Government of India (GoI)'s 50% = Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) 22.5% + Railways 22.5% + NCRPB 5%.

questions.q: Ministry of Railways' share in National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) equity is:
questions.explain: Railways holds 22.5%, equal to Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)'s share.

questions.q: National Capital Region (NCR) Planning Board's share in National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) equity is:
questions.explain: NCRPB holds the smallest Government of India (GoI)-side share — 5%.

questions.q: Each participating state holds what share in National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC)?
questions.explain: 4 states x 12.5% = 50%, matching Government of India (GoI)'s 50%.

questions.q: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC)?
options: Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
questions.explain: The Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) is the ex-officio Chairman of National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC).

questions.q: Who was the first Managing Director of National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC)?
questions.explain: Vinay Kumar Singh became the first Managing Director (MD) in July 2016.

questions.q: Vinay Kumar Singh took over as National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC)'s first Managing Director (MD) in:
questions.explain: The first Managing Director (MD) joined in July 2016, about three years after incorporation.

questions.q: National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC)'s mandate covers which set of activities for Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS)?
options: Design, develop, implement, finance, operate and maintain
questions.explain: National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC)'s mandate is full-cycle: design to finance to operations and maintenance of Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) across National Capital Region (NCR).

questions.q: How many corridors are in Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) Phase-I?
questions.explain: Phase-I has 3 corridors; 8 were identified in the overall Functional Plan — a favourite trap.

questions.q: How many Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) corridors were identified in the National Capital Region (NCR) Functional Plan on Transport-2032?
questions.explain: 8 corridors were identified in the plan; only 3 are being built in Phase-I.

questions.q: Which of these IS a Phase-I Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) corridor?
questions.explain: Phase-I = Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut, Delhi-Gurugram-SNB-Alwar and Delhi-Panipat-Karnal.

questions.q: The Delhi-Gurugram corridor in Phase-I goes up to:
questions.explain: The second Phase-I corridor is Delhi-Gurugram-SNB-Alwar.

questions.q: Which is NOT a Phase-I Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) corridor?
questions.explain: Delhi-Agra is not in Phase-I; Meerut, Alwar and Panipat are.

questions.q: The first Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) corridor, Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut, is how long?
questions.explain: The full corridor is 82.15 km; 17 km was only the priority section.

questions.q: The Delhi-Meerut corridor runs between:
questions.explain: End to end it is Sarai Kale Khan to Modipuram; Sahibabad-Duhai was the priority stretch.

questions.q: The design speed of Namo Bharat trains is:
questions.explain: Design speed 180 kmph — never confuse it with operational 160 or average 100.

questions.q: The maximum operational (service) speed of Namo Bharat trains is:
questions.explain: Operational speed is 160 kmph; 180 is design, 100 is average including stops.

questions.q: The average speed of Namo Bharat services, including stops, is:
questions.explain: Average speed including station stops is 100 kmph.

questions.q: Delhi to Meerut by Namo Bharat takes:
questions.explain: 82.15 km at an average 100 kmph means end-to-end in under 60 minutes.

questions.q: The priority section first opened on the Delhi-Meerut corridor was:
options: 17 km, Sarai Kale Khan to Anand Vihar
questions.explain: The 17 km Sahibabad-Duhai Depot section opened first.

questions.q: The priority section of Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) was inaugurated on:
questions.explain: 20 Oct 2023 — the start of India's first Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) service.

questions.q: The priority section inauguration is historic because it was:
options: India's first Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) service
questions.explain: Sahibabad-Duhai was the first Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) service in India.

questions.q: The track gauge used on Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) is:
questions.explain: Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) uses standard gauge 1,435 mm — broad gauge is the trap option.

questions.q: Conventional Indian Railways mainly uses which gauge?
questions.explain: Mainline IR is mainly broad gauge 1,676 mm, unlike Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS)'s 1,435 mm standard gauge.

questions.q: Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) electrification is:
questions.explain: Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) runs on 25 kV 50 Hz AC overhead electrification, like mainline railways.

questions.q: The signalling system of the Namo Bharat corridor is based on:
options: European Train Control System (ETCS) Level 2 with Hybrid Level 3 over Long Term Evolution (LTE) radio
Track circuit with lineside signals only
questions.explain: European Train Control System (ETCS) L2/Hybrid L3 over Long Term Evolution (LTE) — the world-first ETCS-on-LTE application.

questions.q: What is claimed as a world-first for Namo Bharat signalling?
options: European Train Control System (ETCS) working without radio
ETCS working over Long Term Evolution (LTE) radio
questions.explain: Running European Train Control System (ETCS) over Long Term Evolution (LTE) radio is described as a world-first combination.

questions.q: Platform Screen Doors on Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) are:
options: Provided at every station, integrated with signalling
Not provided; only platform gates at depots
questions.explain: Every Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) station has Platform Screen Doors (PSDs), integrated/synchronised with the signalling and train doors.

questions.q: Besides safety, Platform Screen Doors (PSDs) at Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) stations also help in:
questions.explain: Platform Screen Doors (PSDs) give safety plus air-conditioning efficiency by sealing the platform.

questions.q: The Namo Bharat trainset was designed by Alstom at:
questions.explain: Designed by Alstom at Hyderabad; manufactured at Savli — the two places are a classic swap-trap.

questions.q: The Namo Bharat trainset is manufactured at:
questions.explain: Manufacturing is at Savli, Gujarat; design was at Hyderabad.

questions.q: The Namo Bharat trainset operates with:
options: Automatic Train Operation (ATO) over European Train Control System (ETCS) Level 2
questions.explain: The aerodynamic trainset runs with Automatic Train Operation over European Train Control System (ETCS) L2, supervised by the operator.

questions.q: Operations & Maintenance of the Delhi-Meerut corridor is done by:
options: National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC)'s own station staff union
DB RRTS Operations India Pvt Ltd
questions.explain: Operations and Maintenance (O&M) is with DB RRTS Operations India Pvt Ltd, a Deutsche Bahn subsidiary, under National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) ownership.

questions.q: DB RRTS Operations is a subsidiary of:
questions.explain: Deutsche Bahn (DB) = Deutsche Bahn, the German railway group.

questions.q: The Operations and Maintenance (O&M) contract for the Delhi-Meerut corridor is for:
questions.explain: DB RRTS Operations holds a 12-year Operations and Maintenance (O&M) contract.

questions.q: Meerut Metro is special because it:
options: Shares Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) infrastructure in Meerut — a first in India
questions.explain: For the first time in India, a local metro and a regional Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) share the same corridor infrastructure.

questions.q: Ticketing on Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) uses Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) with:
options: National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) 'One Nation One Card', QR and digital payment
questions.explain: Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) supports National Common Mobility Card (NCMC), QR and digital payment — interoperable with metro and buses.

questions.q: NCMC stands for the concept:
questions.explain: National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) = 'One Nation One Card' for interoperable travel.

questions.q: Earlier, the Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) was called:
questions.explain: The system was earlier branded RapidX; trains/services are now branded Namo Bharat.

questions.q: National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) is often cited as an example of:
questions.explain: Centre and four states sharing equity equally makes National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) a cooperative-federalism example.

questions.q: Compared with a metro, Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) station spacing is typically:
questions.explain: Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) stations are 5-10 km apart typically; metro stations are about 1 km apart.

questions.q: The basic purpose difference between Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) and a metro is:
options: RRTS is regional — connecting satellite towns to the capital; metro is intra-city
RRTS is only for freight; metro is for passengers
RRTS runs inside one city; metro connects states
questions.explain: Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) = regional travel to satellite towns; metro = travel within a city.

questions.q: Where is the corporate headquarters of the National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) located?
questions.explain: The National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) is headquartered in New Delhi — fitting, as it plans and runs regional rail for the National Capital Region (NCR) from the capital.

questions.q: Each Namo Bharat trainset has one special coach designated as:
options: A premium class coach with wider, reclining seats
questions.explain: One coach in every Namo Bharat trainset is a premium class coach, offering wider reclining seats and extra legroom at a higher fare.

questions.q: The Sarai Kale Khan Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) station is planned as a mega multi-modal hub where passengers can interchange with:
options: Delhi Metro, the Hazrat Nizamuddin railway station and the interstate bus terminal
questions.explain: Sarai Kale Khan brings the Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS), Delhi Metro's Pink Line, Hazrat Nizamuddin railway station and the bus terminal together, so passengers can switch modes within one hub.

questions.q: The Delhi–Ghaziabad–Meerut corridor is co-financed by multilateral development banks, namely the:
options: Asian Development Bank (ADB), Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) and New Development Bank (NDB)
questions.explain: The Asian Development Bank (ADB), Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) and New Development Bank (NDB) are funding partners for the corridor, along with the Centre and the state governments.

questions.q: The priority section of the Delhi–Meerut corridor, inaugurated on 20 October 2023, was inaugurated by:
options: The Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh
questions.explain: The Prime Minister inaugurated the Sahibabad–Duhai priority section and flagged off the first Namo Bharat service on 20 October 2023.
